items.prompt: Choose the nominalization of 'We implemented the policy.'
items.explanation: 'Implement' → 'implementation'; the clause becomes a noun phrase.

items.prompt: Write the noun form of 'to decide': Their ___ to expand surprised everyone.
Write the noun form of 'to fail': The system's ___ caused a long outage.
Choose the sentence that uses a denser nominal group.
options: The rapid implementation of the revised policy is expected.
They quickly put the revised policy into effect, which people expect.
The policy was revised, and they implemented it quickly.
It is expected that the revised policy will be put into effect soon.
items.explanation: Nominalization compresses events into one noun phrase.

items.prompt: Which sentence is clearer and stronger?
options: The undertaking of the investigation was conducted with the aim of the establishment of the facts.
An investigation was undertaken by us in order that the facts might be established.
Facts establishment was the aim of the investigation that was undertaken.
items.explanation: Deliberate verbs beat needless nominal chains for clarity.

items.prompt: When does nominalization usually help a sentence?
options: In formal reports that need a neutral, dense register.
In every sentence of casual speech.
Never — it always makes prose worse.
items.explanation: Nominalization suits formal, impersonal register — not all writing.

items.prompt: Write the noun form of 'to refuse': Their ___ to negotiate ended the talks.
